clue.text: Worries over the French game

indicators.note: one word is spread over another, covering it on both sides

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the French and their favourite sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' sits at the end looking like part of the scene, but it is the definition: game as an adjective means plucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Game, as an adjective, means brave and willing to have a go, a synonym for unafraid.

clue.text: Retreat from strong glare

parts.note: F for forte, the musical marking for loud or strong

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from a dazzling light.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a hasty withdrawal or escape, so it is a synonym for a retreat.

clue.text: Suck in stomach muscles or bulge at the front

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: Fitness advice: pull your belly in, or it will stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb something is to take it in, as a sponge sucks up water.

clue.text: Bedridden student has help at university

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
to be up is to be in residence at university, in British usage

explanation.surface: An ill student gets support from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid up is confined to bed through illness or injury.

clue.text: They cannot be criticised for left-wing scares following short dismissal

indicators.note: a word that is cut short loses its final letter
coming after places these pieces behind the dismissal piece

parts.note: the sack is dismissal from a job
red is the colour of the political left
cows as a verb means intimidates

explanation.surface: Political commentary: some people are beyond reproach for scaremongering leftists after a brief sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred cows are ideas or institutions treated as above criticism, an idiom from the Hindu reverence for cattle.

clue.text: Sex information about red

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: going about means turning round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Sex education material concerning communists, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex in the sense of male or female category is a synonym for gender.

clue.text: Minor, yet possibly an atrocious crime

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Something small that might still be a terrible offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the gap between minor and enormous; the strict sense of the word is great wickedness, not great size.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity in its traditional sense is an extremely wicked act or outrage.

clue.text: Give details of French writer

parts.note: a scribe is one who writes

explanation.surface: A request for particulars about an author from France.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of its features.

clue.text: Decided to back loser against current Labour leader

indicators.note: going back means reading from end to start

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the British Labour Party when this was published

explanation.surface: Someone chose to support an underdog in opposition to the Labour leader of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved means having firmly made up one's mind, so it is a synonym for decided.

clue.text: Impulse to sin when drunk can end in court

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A warning that the urge to misbehave while drunk may land you before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate urge to act, a synonym for an impulse.

clue.text: Brags about vessels without topsails

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: split as 'tops' of 'sails': the top of that word in an across entry is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about ships that lack topsails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topsails' is one word in the surface but splits into 'tops' and 'sails' for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to speak with excessive pride, a synonym for brag.

clue.text: Detective's labourer?

parts.note: Hercule Poirot, Agatha Christie's Belgian detective
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A question about who works for a famous sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: the mythical hero performed twelve labours.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was set twelve great labours, so he is jokingly the labourer.

clue.text: Without principles, a doctor comes across really oddly

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of really

explanation.surface: An unscrupulous doctor gives a very strange impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone with no moral sense at all, lacking ethical standards.

clue.text: Interfering half-time director led me so astray

indicators.note: half means only one of the word's two halves survives

parts.note: taken as written; only its back half is kept
D is a standard abbreviation for director

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered out of order

explanation.surface: A football manager poking his nose in at the interval led the team off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddlesome person interferes in others' affairs, so the word is a synonym for interfering.

clue.text: Satisfactory, organised, capable etc

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A school report in three words: good enough, tidy, competent and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable means adequate or good enough, which is what satisfactory conveys.

clue.text: After a zero score girls finished upset

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the score piece

parts.note: a nil score is written as a round zero
F is female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: The girls' team was upset after ending the match without scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Offended means hurt or affronted, a synonym for upset in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Plausible that cheddar rind can be eaten

indicators.note: a rind is the outer skin, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of cheddar

explanation.surface: It is believable that the skin of a cheese is safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Credible means believable, a synonym for plausible.

clue.text: Was sick after enrolled nurse started treatment required

indicators.note: after places the sickness piece behind the nurse and treatment pieces

parts.note: EN is the abbreviation for enrolled nurse

indicators.note: what has only started gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A patient fell ill after a nurse began the treatment they needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Entailed means necessitated or involved as a consequence, so it is a synonym for required.

clue.text: Freshly dawned fair everywhere

indicators.note: freshly suggests making these letters anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A weather report: a newly broken, fine morning across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and wide is an idiom meaning over a great area, in all places.

clue.text: Fame is these days welcomed by non-Western architect

indicators.note: a guest welcomed in is taken inside the host
non-Western means the W for west is dropped

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: An architect from outside the West is becoming celebrated today.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is widespread acclaim and reputation, a synonym for fame.

clue.text: Swimming style is a cause of brain damage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a way of moving through water, such as crawl
second meaning: an interruption of blood supply to the brain

explanation.surface: A health warning that some form of swimming harms the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a swimming technique like backstroke and a cerebral attack caused by a blocked or burst blood vessel.

clue.text: Judge could become weary with Latin

indicators.note: could become suggests the letters may turn into something else

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A judge might grow tired of hearing Latin in court.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain judges are drawn from the legal profession, which makes the definition fair if loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge is a senior member of the legal profession, so a judge is an example of a legal practitioner.

clue.text: Some send earrings to win affection

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to give jewellery as a way of winning someone's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make oneself loved, to win the fondness of others.

clue.text: Doctors detain me for insanity

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A patient complains that physicians are holding them on grounds of madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a plural noun for physicians, but it is a verb meaning falsifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a serious decline in mental faculties, loosely equated with madness.

clue.text: Dip into crowd when Democrat ousts Republican

indicators.note: ousting means one letter is thrown out and another put in its place

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: American politics: dip into a crowd when the Democrats replace the Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble is to take a casual, superficial interest in something, to try it briefly.

clue.text: Tedious repetition of single unvaried sound finally changed

indicators.note: the last letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a monotone is a single unchanging pitch

explanation.surface: Boredom from one dull note that eventually alters.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of the noun becomes a Y, turning the sound into the state of dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is wearisome sameness, the dullness of something repeated without variation.

clue.text: Has great fear of wild adders

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are running out of control

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified of snakes in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to anticipate it with great fear.

clue.text: Rudolph and friends said it was wet 'ere

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and judged by their sound

parts.note: it was wet here, in dropped-aitch speech

explanation.surface: Santa's team grumble about the weather where they landed.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ere signals a Cockney accent: 'rained 'ere'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph is the red-nosed member of Santa's sleigh team, so he and his friends are the herd that pulls it.
